title: PPA-Game: Characterizing and Learning Competitive Dynamics Among Online Content Creators

problem.claim: Agents compete for divisible resources with payoffs determined proportionately by heterogeneous agent weights, modeling online content creators competing for finite consumer attention.

gap.claim: The abstract does not state a specific prior-work gap; it frames the work as analyzing both static competitive payoffs and online learning about resource payoffs.

contributions.claim: Introduces the Proportional Payoff Allocation Game for characterizing competition among agents over divisible resources.
Provides a game-theoretical analysis of pure Nash equilibrium existence and identifies scenarios that ensure existence.
Integrates a multi-player multi-armed bandit framework and proposes an online algorithm for maximizing cumulative payoffs over T rounds.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Simulated experiments report that cases without a pure Nash equilibrium rarely occur.
Theoretical analysis reports that each agent's regret is bounded by O(log^1 + η T) for any η > 0.
Empirical results report that the online learning approach is effective.

narrative_sequence.summary: Introduces the PPA-Game for competition over divisible resources with proportionate payoffs based on heterogeneous weights.
Relates the game dynamics to online content creators competing for finite consumer attention under quality-dependent exposure.
Analyzes pure Nash equilibrium existence and reports that nonexistence cases are rare in simulations.
Extends the setting to online learning with a multi-player multi-armed bandit framework and proposes an algorithm for cumulative payoff maximization.
Reports a logarithmic regret bound and empirical validation of the online learning approach.

source_observation.claim: The model represents resource competition through proportionate payoffs with heterogeneous weights.

interpretation.claim: Competitive allocation models can capture differentiated agent quality or influence while preserving shared-resource competition.

application.claim: This modeling pattern may support analysis of creator competition for attention on recommender systems.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that the model applies beyond the described online-content setting.

source_observation.claim: The work combines equilibrium analysis with online learning and reports a regret bound for the learning process.

interpretation.claim: Static strategic analysis and adaptive learning analysis can be treated as complementary views of the same competitive system.

application.claim: A system designer could evaluate both equilibrium behavior and cumulative-payoff learning when studying adaptive competition.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify the assumptions or practical conditions under which the regret guarantee applies.

unknowns: The abstract does not identify the specific prevalent scenarios that guarantee pure Nash equilibrium existence.
The abstract does not provide the regret-bound exponent formatting, algorithm details, experimental settings, baselines, or datasets.
